name: Large fire extinguisher
description: A heavy red cylinder of firefighting foam with a squeeze lever and a hose. Puts out a fire beside you.
notes: Standing upright, label on +z: a 170 mm cylinder 380 mm to the shoulder, a brass valve with carry handle, squeeze lever and gauge, and a hose down the +x side to a nozzle clipped low on the body. `extinguishing` is a new quality name; the large one takes the higher level. The charge of foam and the use action are left to the tool framework.

name: Fire axe
description: A two-handed axe with a red head: a broad blade on one side and a spike on the other for breaking through doors and glass. A slow, heavy weapon.
notes: Lies flat along x with the head at +x, blade on +z and pick on -z, gripped near the butt. CHECK VOLUME is the T shape: the box is mostly air around the haft and head. `chopping` is a new quality name for axe work. Melee stats are left for tuning: it should hit like the sledgehammer but cut, and recover slowly. The reference's negative butchering is not carried over.

name: Halligan bar
description: A heavy steel forcing bar with a forked claw at one end and an adze and spike at the other. Opens a locked door without wrecking it, lifts manhole covers and makes a brutal club.
notes: Lies flat along x: fork at -x, adze on +z and pike on -z at +x, knurled grip rings near the fork end. Drawn from an 845 mm sketch scaled by 0.9 to the reference's 760 mm. CHECK VOLUME: the reference's 550 ml is the steel, while the box measures the T of the head. `digging` is a new quality name; the reference's nail-pulling is covered by prying.

name: Pike pole
description: A long yellow fibreglass pole with a rubber grip and a steel head: a straight spike and a hook curving back. For pulling down ceilings and reaching things at a distance.
notes: Lies flat along x with the head at +x and the hook on +z. CHECK VOLUME is the long thin pole. No fibreglass finish exists, so the shaft is `plastic-yellow`. `hooking` is a new quality name; the reference's cooking quality looks like an error and is not carried over. The bomb-disposal hot stick shares this model: an insulated pole of the same build and weight with a hooked head.

name: Hot stick
description: A long insulated fibreglass pole with a hooked steel head, for moving a suspect package or a live wire from a safe distance.
notes: A variant of the pike pole on its model at the same 3.1 kg; same shape and finishes.

name: Small fire extinguisher
description: A red carbon dioxide extinguisher you can carry in one hand, with a squeeze lever and a black discharge horn on a short hose.
notes: Standing upright, label on +z: a 100 mm cylinder with a steel valve, squeeze lever and gauge, and a hose down the +x side to a black horn clipped to the body. Held upright in the hand. The gas charge and use action are left to the tool framework.

name: Throwable fire extinguisher
description: A red steel ball of fire suppressant with a pull plug on top. Heat sets it off, so you throw it into the flames from a distance.
notes: Standing on its ball: an 84 mm red steel sphere with a white label band, a short neck, a black cap and a steel pull ring. It is used up by throwing, so it brings no tool quality; the thrown burst is left to the framework. The reference's 250 ml fits the ball; the box ratio counts the neck and ring.

name: Bottle fish trap
description: Two plastic bottles made into a trap: the top of one is cut off and pushed neck first into the other, so a fish that swims in after the bait cannot find its way out.
notes: Lies along x: a two-litre bottle 270 mm long with its top cut off and turned back inside as a funnel at +x, tied in with cord, a cord along the top for setting it and a few drain holes. The tiles draw the clear plastic opaque, so the inner funnel shows only as its rim; in the game it stays see-through. `fish_trapping` is a new quality name. Setting it in water and catching fish are left to the framework.

name: Wicker fish trap
description: A long woven cone of reeds bound with bark hoops, with a funnel in its mouth. Fish swim in after the bait and cannot find the way back out.
notes: Lies along x: a wicker cone 500 mm long and 240 mm across its mouth at +x, closed and tied at -x, with an inner reed funnel in the mouth and four bark hoops and a rim. No woven finish exists, so the weave is suggested by stepped rings in `straw-wicker`.
